<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par133 />{{GHGmargin-letter|133|f}}
'''2.''' The correlative comparatives ''greater—less'' (''older—younger'') are expressed by the simple adjective with the article (''the great'', equivalent to ''the greater'', &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=31.34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=16.18.26|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|g}}
'''3.''' To express the ''superlative'' it is also sufficient (see above, ''f'') to make the adjective determinate, either by means of the article or a following partitive genitive (or suffix); in this case the article or genitive indicates that the attribute in question belongs especially to one or more definite individuals;<ref>Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עֶלְיוֹן|translate=the one above}}, i.e. ''the Most High''.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הַצְּעִרָה|translate=the least}}; 16:11 {{GHGheb|text=הַקָּטָן|translate=the little one}}, i.e. the ''youngest'' of eight sons; 17:14 ''David was'' {{GHGheb|text=הַקָּטָן}} ''the youngest, and the three great'', i.e. elder, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=8}}.—So also with a qualifying adjective, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּנוֹ הַקָּטָן|translate=his youngest son}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=15}}; also with a following genitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=21|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹן בָּנָיו|translate=the youngest of his sons}}: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=24}} ''the least upon the earth''; with suffix, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=טוֹבָם|translate=their good one}}, i.e. the best of them; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=3|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=מִגְּדוֹלָם וְעַד־קְטַנָּם|translate=from the greatest of them even to the least of them}}; cf. the inverse order in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=34|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|h}}
Rem. 1. The above examples apply only to the most common ''relative'' attributes (''great, small, good''), and to expressions which by usage easily came to be recognized as periphrases for the superlative. Other adjectives, however, when followed by a partitive genitive, also acquire the sense of a superlative; this appears from the context, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=19}} ''the most hidden treasures of the sand''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=29}} ''the wisest amongst her ladies''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=8|hidebook=1}} f., 29:19, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=6}} (''in the most horrible of valleys''), 41:22; probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16}}. On this government by the adjective generally, cf. {{GHGpar|132|c}}.—Moreover, the combination of a substantive in the construct state with an adjective used substantivally ({{GHGpar|128|w}}) sometimes serves as a periphrasis for the superlative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל כְּלֵי הַקָּטָן|translate=all the smallest vessels}}. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=7|verse=10}} see {{GHGpar|126|x}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|i}}
2. Other periphrases for the superlative are the use of a substantive in the construct state before the plural of the same word (which is naturally to be regarded as a partitive genitive; cf. our ''book of books''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים|translate=the most holy place}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=1}}) ''the most excellent song''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=25}} (= ''servus servorum, the lowest servant''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=17}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=136|verse=2}}, 3)<ref>''God of gods, and Lord of lords'', just as the supreme god of the Babylonians is called ''bēl bēlī'' (Tiele, ''Compend. der Rel.-Gesch.'', p. 87).</ref>; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=10}} (cf. Gal 1:5, Rev 22:5); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=7|hidebook=1}} (''king of kings'', of Nebuchadrezzar; cf. 1 Tim 6:15, Rev 17:14, 19:16, and another kind of periphrasis in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=3}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=2}}. Similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=28}} two participles are combined, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=15}} two substantives in the singular. Finally, the same object is attained by connecting one substantive in the construct state with another of the same stem ({{GHGheb|text=שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן|translate=a sabbath of solemn rest}}, i.e. an obligatory day of rest, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=15}}, &c.) or of the same meaning (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=ח֫שֶׁךְ אֲפֵלָה|translate=a thick darkness}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=22}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|k}}
3. The intensification of attributes by means of repetition belongs rather to rhetoric than to syntax, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=עָמֹק עָמֹק|translate=exceeding deep}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=14}}; the adjective is even used three times in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=3}}.—Cf. the repetition of adverbs for the same purpose in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְאֹד מְאֹד|translate=exceedingly}}, also {{GHGheb|text=בִּמְאֹד מְאֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=7}}, &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=42|verse=15}}.—On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=43}} the repetition expresses<section end=par133 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
